bull.b: A secured, multi-decade Anthropic contract provides rare long-term revenue visibility for an infrastructure developer. Contracted cash flows de-risk commercialization of power-advantaged sites, support financing for staged buildouts, and materially reduce exposure to volatile Bitcoin mining revenue.

bull.t: Pivot to contracted HPC leasing with high adjusted margins
bull.b: Rapid ramp in HPC lease revenue and very high adjusted margins indicate a structurally more profitable business model than commodity mining. Contracted, multi‑year leases with near‑asset economics should drive durable adjusted EBITDA improvement and lower earnings volatility over time.

bull.t: Large liquidity and funded development pipeline ($3.1B cash)
bull.b: Substantial cash and restricted cash provide a multi‑year runway to fund capital-intensive campus buildouts without immediate market financing. This funding cushion reduces execution financing risk, allows measured capital deployment, and supports transition from mining to contracted HPC revenue.

bear.b: Negative trailing equity and prior episodes of extreme leverage weaken financial resilience. Persistent equity deficits constrain borrowing capacity, increase cost of capital, complicate covenant negotiations, and heighten dependence on external financing or asset monetization to support growth.

bear.t: Consistent negative operating and free cash flow
bear.b: Sustained operating cash burn and deeply negative free cash flow indicate the core business does not self-fund expansion. Over time this raises dilution or refinancing risk, forces asset sales or JV monetizations, and increases vulnerability if capital markets tighten during multi-year buildouts.

bear.t: Customer / revenue concentration from large Anthropic deal
bear.b: While lucrative, heavy reliance on a single large tenant concentrates counterparty and renegotiation risk. Delivery delays, contractual disputes, or tenant financial stress would disproportionately affect cash flows; concentration also links company performance tightly to one customer’s demand timeline.
